_meta.description: Authoring source-of-truth for the DEDICATED ages-4-9 Bible-retelling lane (the gentle, simple-sentence product defined by docs/KID_STORY_PROMPT.md). One entry per story file under assets/stories/parable_*_kid*.txt.
_meta.notImpactedBy: This lane is SEPARATE from the 115 'kidFriendly: true' entries in manifest.json. Those are regular adult Traditional stories merely flagged kid-safe (full adult prose + audio). Do NOT conflate the two.
statusLifecycle: PROPOSED  - anchor chosen, not yet written
REVIEW    - written, needs editorial pass against KID_STORY_PROMPT.md
NEEDS_REWRITE - written but fails a rule (scripture/safety/length); see notes
REJECTED  - off-prompt (wrong approach), kept as training artifact, will not ship
SUPERSEDED - right approach but replaced by a doctrine-v2 telling; file kept, not pejorative; terminal/non-counting like REJECTED
APPROVED  - passes editorial; ready for audio
AUDIO_PENDING - approved, audio not yet rendered
DONE      - approved + audio rendered + promoted into manifest.json
_meta.promotion: Stories at status DONE are mirrored into assets/stories/manifest.json (kidFriendly: true) by scripts/promote_kid_stories.py.
_meta.lengthNote: Kid word bands (Adam 2026-06-15) — serve the child, not the adult corpus. Replace the adult floors (short 300-500 / full 501-900), which were too long for gentle 4-7 bedtime prose and created a 'pad to satisfy the validator' incentive. short+full overlap 400-450 on purpose; pick by intent. Don't pad. Legacy time-bucket values (3min/5min/etc.) are gone; legacy stories still carry those lengthBucket strings until migrated.

stories.title: Jairus' Little Girl
stories.reflectionQuestion: When you don't feel well, who do you like to have close to you?
stories.kidSafetyNotes: Hurting->hope. Death handled gently: Jesus says she is 'only sleeping' and wakes her (faithful to Mark 5:39). Bleeding-woman subplot omitted. One indelible image (held): Jesus takes her hand, 'it's time to get up'.

stories.title: The Walls of Jericho
stories.reflectionQuestion: What do you think it was like to march around those great walls so quietly, day after day, waiting?
stories.kidSafetyNotes: Joshua 6 adapted for ages 4-7 (Adam 2026-06-15): conquest/killing OMITTED entirely. Reframed from 'God has given us the city' / 'walked into the city' (dispossession) to Joshua shouting 'God is with us!' + a wonder ending ('all the things God could do'). Theme = TRUSTING God before you see anything happen (the quiet marching, the waiting). 'God is with us!' ties to the not-alone spine (faithful: the ark/God's presence is carried around Jericho). One image: the walls tumbling flat. Texture: kinetic/exterior/sound (marching, trumpets, shout, crash).

stories.title: Joseph Forgives His Brothers
stories.reflectionQuestion: What do you think Joseph felt when he saw his brothers again, after so many years away?
stories.kidSafetyNotes: Backstory softened (brothers 'jealous, sent him far away'; pit + slavery OMITTED); no violence. KEY THEOLOGY (Adam 2026-06-15, see feedback_kid_god_with_not_cause): 'God was still working for good' NOT 'God turned it into something good' -- God WITH Joseph in the sad thing, never the cause of it. A literal 5-year-old must not hear 'God made Joseph sad on purpose.' Not-alone spine ('God never once left his side'). One image: Joseph weeping as he embraces the brothers who wronged him. Adam: A+.

stories.title: The Cross
stories.reflectionQuestion: What do you think it means to be loved as much as Jesus loves you?
stories.kidSafetyNotes: THE hard story, told via the Joseph method (feedback_kid_god_with_not_cause). LOVE-centered, not suffering-centered: death stated softly ('his breath grew still'); NO nails/blood/gore. Jesus's real words kept ('Father, forgive them'; 'into your hands'). Names that God had NOT left ('there in the dark') and refuses to end in the dark -- ends forward ('Sunday was coming'), gently pointing to Easter (1812). Grounding image: his mother Mary among the watchers (threads to 1824). Mood=hurting: the comfort for a sad child is 'Jesus knows sadness, loves you this much, and God did not leave.' Adam: braver-set centerpiece; reviewed line-by-line.

stories.title: God Calls Abraham
stories.reflectionQuestion: What do you think it was like for Abraham to set out, not yet knowing where God was leading him?
stories.kidSafetyNotes: Trust before you can see: God calls Abraham to a land he can't yet see; Abraham goes. Gentle, no peril. Center = 'he did not know the way ahead, but he knew the One who was leading him.' Grounding: tents under a sky of more stars than he could count (Gen 12 call + the stars promise). Mood calm_peaceful (quiet trust on the journey). Part of the not-alone spine -- God beside him every step.

Threads to 1821 -- the same Mary who says yes to the baby stands by him at the cross.

One image: the boy's five loaves + two fish feeding everyone, with baskets left over. Texture = crowds / daylight / grassy hillside (kinetic-exterior, counters quiet-room drift). Center: God does much with a little freely given. Mood grateful (provision + thankfulness).

stories.title: The Lost Sheep
stories.reflectionQuestion: What do you think the little sheep felt when it heard the shepherd's voice say, 'I found you'?
stories.kidSafetyNotes: PARABLE -- Jesus's teaching picture; frame made explicit at the close (Adam edit): 'God loves you, just like that good shepherd loved his one little sheep,' so kids know it's a picture, not a literal sheep-hunt. The SIGNATURE story for the lane's confirmed 'God is with me / not alone' spine in its tenderest form: 'when I wander, God comes looking for me.' The lost sheep is alone/afraid but NOT in danger (no predators -- keep it about lostness + love, not peril). One image: carried home on the shepherd's shoulders. Supersedes legacy kid_502_lostsheep_short.

stories.title: The Wise and Foolish Builders
stories.reflectionQuestion: What do you think it felt like inside the strong house on the rock, while the storm blew all around outside?
stories.kidSafetyNotes: PARABLE. Pairs with 1816 (Jesus Calms the Storm): 1816 = 'Jesus is with you IN the storm,' this = 'build on Jesus BEFORE the storm.' Sand house washes away GENTLY -- no one in it, no scary collapse ('slowly, quietly, the little house slipped away'). KEY theology edit (Adam): 'strong and STEADY' not 'strong and safe' -- obedience gives steadiness THROUGH storms, never a guarantee bad things won't come (see feedback_kid_god_with_not_cause / faithful_not_gentle). Wise builder 'she' / foolish 'he' (gender variety). Promoted to short+full (storm drama earns it). One image: two houses in the storm, one standing, one washing away.

stories.title: The Tiny Mustard Seed
stories.reflectionQuestion: What do you think the little birds felt, building their nests high in the branches of that great and beautiful tree?
stories.kidSafetyNotes: PARABLE. SHORT-ONLY by design -- a 2-verse parable; a 'full' would require padding (honor its brevity, per length-bucket doctrine). 'God grows small things into something great and good and beautiful.' Gentle, no peril. One image: the seed too small to see -> the great tree with birds nesting in its branches.

stories.title: The Night in Bethlehem
stories.reflectionQuestion: What do you think it was like in that quiet stable, the night the baby Jesus was born?
stories.kidSafetyNotes: The NATIVITY -- a cornerstone the lane lacked (had wise_men 1809, not the birth itself). Hushed/peaceful telling (shepherds + angels are separate anchors, not here), tagged calm_peaceful to match the quiet holy-night register (bedtime-perfect). Same VOICE_MARY_PONDER as 1824 (Mary Says Yes) -- deliberate continuity, the same 'Mary' voice through both Mary stories. 'No room' kept gentle; stable cozy not grim. Luke 2:19 'held it in her heart' echo, softened ending. One image: baby Jesus asleep in the manger on the hay.

stories.title: Water into Wine
stories.reflectionQuestion: What do you think the servants felt when the plain water they had poured turned out to be something wonderful?
stories.kidSafetyNotes: Jesus's FIRST miracle. 'Wine' kept gentle as 'the very best, most delicious drink' -- it's the wedding-feast drink; no alcohol focus (kid-appropriate softening, like 'The Big Picnic' for feeding_5000). Festive/joyful texture (wedding, music, celebration) -- counterweight to the 3 quiet parables in this batch. Mary's line kept ('Whatever he tells you to do, just do it'). FRESH voice VOICE_CHARLOTTE_V3 (first use in the kid lane). Promoted to short+full (full wedding scene earns it). One image: six empty stone jars filled with water -> poured out as something wonderful.
